body.prompt:
Use case: ChandRush Chapter 03 location reference plate S03-D04, the same safe ribbon bench and model stand in the Elephant Work Bay after the thirty plain ivory ribbons have been shared into the BLUE tray (twelve) and the GOLD tray (eighteen), with the checked plan beside the small elephant model. Later plates reuse this bench, the colouring mat, the open colour case and the plan, and every count and inscription must be exact.
Asset: one 4:3 landscape scenic image of an empty location, no characters.
Input images:
- Image 1: the approved plate S03-D03, the same ribbon bench before sharing. Use it for: the exact design, materials and finish of the cream stone ribbon bench and the adjoining model stand (indigo trestles, brass corners), the shallow open ribbon box, the BLUE tray with blue-painted rim and the GOLD tray with gold-painted rim, the plain ivory notched silk ribbons, the small cream tray cards on little stands, the small blue elephant model on four small wheels, the rolled yellow measuring tape, the gold-posted visitor rope with blue rope line, the background (machinery rail, the large blue elephant float partly visible, lanterns, arcades, one full moon) and the pale wet paving. Ignore: the ribbons lying in the box in three rows (they are now moved), the old design card "BLUE : GOLD 2 : 3" (not present now), the old tray-card words, the trolley and the loading board (both are outside this frame), and any camera detail that conflicts with the framing below.
Camera and framing: 4:3 medium three-quarter view at standing eye height, about 2.5 metres from the benches, looking down about 35 degrees from the near crew side, similar to Image 1 but shifted slightly so that both tables are well inside the frame. The ribbon bench fills the central and right foreground; the model stand adjoins it at screen-left, slightly further back. The visitor rope runs through the lower-left corner. The loading board and the trolley are outside this frame. Both tables show their trestle legs and brass corners.
Place and construction: on the ribbon bench top, in one row from screen-left to screen-right: the BLUE tray (blue-painted rim), the original shallow ribbon box in the middle (open, now empty), and the GOLD tray (gold-painted rim), with small gaps between them, the same designs as Image 1; the trays are a little longer than in Image 1 so that groups of ribbons fit in a single flat layer. A small cream tray card stands on a little stand at the near edge in front of each tray: the card is about one eighth of the frame width wide and has a wide blank cream margin below its text. At the rear-right corner of the bench top lies the colouring mat, a flat rectangular protective mat of soft grey-blue felt with a brass-studded edge, and beside it on the same corner stands an open colour case: a low timber case with its lid propped open at the back, holding two small round paint pots (one blue paint, one gold paint, both with their lids on) and one slim paintbrush that rests inside the case along its edge. The model stand carries the small blue elephant model (one fifth the size of the real float: same blue timber body, brass trim and red-and-gold parade cloth, on four small wheels) and, standing upright beside it on a small brass easel, a large flat cream plan sheet about one third of the frame width wide, held in a thin brass frame, carrying three lines of printed text (see inscriptions). The model's wheels are small and original. A rolled yellow measuring tape lies flat as a small coil on the model stand, away from the model and clear of the plan sheet; it has no numerals.
State at this moment (exact):
1. BLUE tray: exactly 12 (twelve) ivory ribbons in total, arranged as exactly 2 (two) separated groups of exactly 6 (six) ribbons each. Each group is a neat flat block of 2 rows of 3 ribbons in one single layer, with a clear empty gap of bare tray floor between the two groups and no overlaps. Do not show 11, 13 or any other number.
2. GOLD tray: exactly 18 (eighteen) ivory ribbons in total, arranged as exactly 3 (three) separated groups of exactly 6 (six) ribbons each. Each group is a neat flat block of 2 rows of 3 ribbons in one single layer, with clear gaps between the three groups and no overlaps. Do not show 17, 19 or any other number.
3. All ribbons are plain ivory (no blue, no gold, no marks). The original ribbon box in the middle is completely empty: no ribbon in it and none on the bench top outside the trays. The total is exactly 12 plus 18 equals 30 ribbons.
4. The colouring mat is clear and empty: nothing at all lies on it. The brush rests inside the open colour case. The case and mat stand at the rear-right corner, clear of all ribbons and of the plan sheet.
5. The plan sheet and the model are on the model stand beside the ribbon bench, the tape is a rolled coil on the model stand.
6. The near bench edge in front of the tray cards is clear open cream stone.
Physical inscriptions (render exactly, nothing else): the card in front of the BLUE tray reads on one line "BLUE 12" and the card in front of the GOLD tray reads on one line "GOLD 18", each in bold dark capitals, the two-digit number as large as the word, text about one tenth of the frame width wide, with the card's lower margin blank. The plan sheet carries exactly three lines of bold dark printed text, one under another, each on one line and large and sharp: "BODY 60 cm → 300 cm, ×5" then "WHEEL 8 cm → 40 cm" then "STRAP 30 cm → 150 cm". Use a true right-pointing arrow → and a true multiplication sign × (not the letter x); the letters "cm" are lowercase; the numbers are exactly 60, 300, 5, 8, 40, 30, 150. No other words, letters or numbers anywhere: the ribbons, box, trays, case, paint pots, mat, model, tape, tables and paving carry no writing.
Keep clear and visible: the clear near bench edge in front of the tray cards (the blank card margins); the protected mat beside the open colour case; the clear edge of the plan sheet; the groups of six in both trays; the model stand.
Light: warm amber from the fixed lanterns and arcade lights; cool full-moon light on brass, stone and ivory silk; crisp contact shadows.
Do not show: any person, child, hand or animal; a ribbon in the central box; ribbons in a heap, overlapping or not in groups of six; a ribbon on the mat; blue or gold ribbons; any other numbers or words; the trolley; any painted title, frame, white label or arrow.

Look and finish (same for every ChandRush location plate): premium semi-realistic painterly 2.5D graphic-novel illustration that matches the supplied ChandRush masters, a blend of illustration and reality. It is painterly in finish but crisp and precise in drawing. Materials and light have near-photographic conviction while forms stay clean, idealised and orderly, like a high-end storybook. ChandRush is an ancient travelling fair with grand, mystic, magical scale and real architectural detailing: dimensional deep-indigo and ultramarine painted timber with visible grain, joinery, rivets and edge banding; warm polished and cast brass with bright specular edges and a light patina; pale cream stone worktops and pale irregular stone paving with a light wet sheen and crisp reflections; layered fabric canopies; restrained circular celestial ornament (full-moon discs, rings, small eight-point stars) in gold and brass. Palette: ultramarine, cobalt, indigo and navy against amber, honey-gold and brass, with strong warm-cool contrast, saturated but natural, never neon. Light: fixed amber task lamps cast clean, well-defined warm pools, their glow held tight around the lamp glass with no spreading halo; cool full-moon light edges roofs, canopy gaps, stone and brass; deep, rich shadows that keep readable detail. Clarity: clear, dry night air with no haze, fog, mist, smoke or airborne dust. Crisp edges and high micro-contrast. Sharp, clean textures in wood grain, brass and stone, as in a high-resolution photograph. True deep darks and clean colours, never a milky, washed-out or glowing veil over the image, never soft focus. The background stays crisp and only slightly darker with distance. Ornament is dense above eye level and on frames; floors, worktops and mechanisms stay open, clean and readable.

Production rules (apply to every plate):
- Frame: one 4:3 landscape scenic image filling the whole canvas edge to edge. No border, title band, panel frame, vignette box or blank margin.
- Lettering: the only lettering allowed is the physical inscriptions listed above, rendered exactly as written, letter for letter, with each minus sign as a true minus sign. No other words, numbers or symbols anywhere. No title, caption, callout, label box, leader line, arrow, legend, watermark or signature: titles and callouts are added later by the production team.
- Reference images: their titles, annotation words, label boxes and arrows only identify places for you. Reproduce none of them.
- Empty location: no people, children, helpers, animals, hands, shadows of figures or silhouettes, and no standing or seated figure of any kind. The only figure permitted is one that the prompt itself describes as a flat painted picture on a stand. The place waits, ready for characters to be added later.
- Counts and states are exact as stated. Add no extra copies of any counted object and no extra devices, cards, lamps or tiles.
- Unlit means unlit: clear or smoky glass with no flame, no inner glow and no bloom. Lit lamps glow only at their own glass.
- Avoid: haze, fog, mist, bloom halos, soft focus, a low-contrast or milky wash, modern signage, plastic, neon, sci-fi screens, crowds, text on fabric or banners, mirrored or garbled lettering, duplicated objects, warped or melted geometry, a second moon in the sky, a crescent moon.

Use case: ChandRush Chapter 03 location reference plate S03-D12, the costume trolley with its lid still closed, its leading wheels partway down the short loading board beside the ribbon bench in the Elephant Work Bay. Later plates reuse this trolley position, the board and the bay, so every fitting must be clear.
Asset: one 4:3 landscape scenic image of an empty location, no characters.
Input images:
- Image 1: the approved plate S03-D03, the ribbon bench area of the Elephant Work Bay. Use it for: the design of the ribbon bench and model stand (cream stone on indigo trestles, brass corners), the short timber loading board beside the bench, the fixed indigo-and-brass machinery rail, the blue elephant float on blocked small wheels, the wheel rack, the lanterns, arcades and the one full moon, and the pale wet paving. Ignore: its camera, the ribbon box contents, the design card text, the trolley's exact position (here it has moved onto the board) and the brake state (here it is released).
- Image 2: the approved plate S02-B01, the open costume trolley. Use it for: the exact design of the trolley (light red timber frame, four small wheels with brass hubs, a straight brass side handle fixed on one end, a low blue costume box with brass corner straps, a brass clasp and a gold sun emblem on its front, a fixed blue rack above with a red cushion below and a blue cushion on top held by two brown leather straps, and the brass-and-timber brake lever on the camera-facing side below the box rim). Ignore: its open lid and the box contents (here the lid is closed and latched), the bench at its left, and its raised-lever pose details beyond what is stated below.
Camera and framing: 4:3 low three-quarter view from the level crew apron beside the short board, camera height about 1.2 metres, about 3 metres from the trolley, looking along the side of the trolley. The trolley is the main subject in the centre and screen-right of centre, fully inside the frame with all four wheels, its side handle, brake lever and cushion rack visible. The short loading board runs from the level parking patch at the screen-left, beside the ribbon bench, gently down towards the bay at screen-right. In the background at the left, the cream ribbon bench and model stand with the small elephant model are visible on their trestles, with the colouring mat and open colour case on the bench's rear corner. At the right-rear the fixed machinery rail and the large blue elephant float on its small blocked wheels are visible, with the lit arcades, lanterns and one full moon behind. Level paving in the foreground in front of the trolley is open and clear.
Place and construction: the short board is a plain timber ramp, broad enough for the trolley's wheel tracks, whose upper end meets the level parking patch of paving beside the ribbon bench and whose lower end ends well short of the blocked elephant wheels. The side apron beside it is level paving. The trolley is the S02-B01 design: it travels lengthways down the board, its brass side handle fixed at its uphill (screen-left) end. Its camera-facing side carries the hand-operated brake lever below the box rim, near the leading wheel pair. The box rim is low, only about 20 centimetres above the paving, lower than the bench top. The two leading wheels are on the board, partway down the slope; the two rear wheels remain near the level top of the board. The trolley is therefore tilted very slightly forward, only a few degrees, matching the shallow board.
State at this moment (exact):
1. Trolley: one wheel position only, no motion blur, no ghost copies; exactly four wheels, all firmly touching the board or level paving.
2. Lid: closed and latched by the brass clasp, flat over the box; no cloth, sleeve or garment hangs out or lies on the trolley.
3. Brake: released; the lever is raised and pushed up and away from the wheel, not pressing the wheel.
4. Cushions: two (red below, blue above) strapped on the fixed rack, not moving.
5. Handle: the fixed brass side handle is clear and unobstructed.
6. Blocked elephant float in the background, original small wheels with chock blocks, thick support strap taut, final red strap loose and unfitted.
7. On the distant ribbon bench: the rear-corner colouring mat carries one ivory ribbon that is partly blue (its half nearest one end painted blue, the other half plain ivory), the paintbrush rests in the open colour case beside it.
8. The paving beside the handle and under the trolley's path is clear.
Physical inscriptions: none. No letters, numbers or symbols anywhere: the card, trays, plan sheet, trolley, box and board carry no readable writing.
Keep clear and visible: the level paving beside the handle on the apron side; the side handle; the fixed trolley frame beside the leading wheel (clear of the wheel); the brake lever; the whole board with the leading wheels on it.
Light: warm amber from the fixed lanterns and arcade lights; cool full-moon light on brass edges and stone; crisp contact shadows.
Do not show: any person, child, hand or animal; an open lid; a sleeve hanging out; an engaged (lowered) brake; more or fewer than four wheels; motion ghosts or repeated trolley positions; a second trolley; the painted title, frame, white label boxes or arrows from any reference.
